claims.text: Sentry — Hallucination: A counterfeit has the form without the power. It is exposed by a discerning sensor or by testing its effect, and it collapses under real force. Residual: Hallucinations are the Protoss's own decoys, so the counterfeiter here is the established-order faction, not the adversary. The structural point (form without power, test by effect) is unchanged, but the moral role is not carried over. 2 Timothy 3:5 describes people, not apparitions.

## SC-SCA-DISC-001: StarCraft abilities: counterfeit, concealment and discernment

Request: Shax t587u (2026-11-25). Catalogue: docs/STARCRAFT_ABILITY_THEOLOGY_MAP.md. Evidence: docs/evidence/starcraft-abilities/abilities.jsonl.

### Invariant
Two kinds of hiding need two kinds of seeing. Concealed presence and counterfeit form are exposed by a specialist sensor that some members have and the whole body depends on. A counterfeit in the community's own form (the Changeling) is not exposed by any sensor, only by its fruit and by its failure to answer the shepherd's command.

Texts: Num 22:23-31; 2 Kgs 6:17; 1 Cor 12:10, 12:21; 2 Tim 3:5; Exod 7:11-12; 2 Cor 11:14; 1 John 4:1; Matt 7:15-20; John 10:4-5, 10:14

### STRONG rows

#### SC2-P06 — Sentry: Hallucination [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Creates copies of Protoss units that look real to the enemy, deal no damage, cannot use abilities, die easily, and are revealed by detectors.
- Counterpart (text): The appearance of godliness without its power; the magicians' imitation staffs swallowed by the real one; Satan disguised as an angel of light; test the spirits.
- Citation: 2 Tim 3:5; Exod 7:11-12; 2 Cor 11:14; 1 John 4:1
- Invariant (interpretation): A counterfeit has the form without the power. It is exposed by a discerning sensor or by testing its effect, and it collapses under real force.
- Residual: Hallucinations are the Protoss's own decoys, so the counterfeiter here is the established-order faction, not the adversary. The structural point (form without power, test by effect) is unchanged, but the moral role is not carried over. 2 Timothy 3:5 describes people, not apparitions.
- Sources: sc2/Sentry (Legacy of the Void)

#### BW-P02 — High Templar: Hallucination [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Creates two copies of a target unit with timed life that take double damage and deal none.
- Counterpart (text): Appearance without power.
- Citation: 2 Tim 3:5; Exod 7:11-12
- Invariant (interpretation): A counterfeit has form without power and collapses under real force.
- Residual: As SC2-P06. In Brood War the copies can be made of any target unit, which strengthens the counterfeit reading.
- Sources: bw/High Templar

#### SC2-Z06 — Overseer: Spawn Changeling [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Spawns a no-attack unit that, on seeing an enemy, takes that race's basic form and team colour (Marine, Zealot or Zergling). It is not auto-attacked. No form of detection exposes it. It is revealed when the owner selects it and cannot give it orders, finds no selection circle when boxing the army, or notices that it never fights.
- Counterpart (text): False prophets in sheep's clothing, known by their fruits; the stranger the sheep do not follow, and the shepherd who knows his own.
- Citation: Matt 7:15-20; John 10:4-5, 10:14; Matt 7:21-23
- Invariant (interpretation): An impostor in the community's own form cannot be exposed by sensing. It is exposed by what it does (no fruit) and by whether it answers the shepherd (it will not take orders).
- Residual: In Matthew 7 the wolf is ravenous; the Changeling is harmless and only spies. The test (fruit, and response to the owner's command) is the matching part, and it is load-bearing in both. In John 10 the sheep refuse the stranger; here the stranger cannot receive the shepherd's command, which is the same relation seen from the other side.
- Sources: sc2/Overseer (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Changeling (Legacy of the Void)

#### PASS-03 — Observer, Overseer, Raven, Science Vessel, Overlord (BW), Missile Turret, Spore Crawler, Photon Cannon; Scanner Sweep: Detection [STRONG]
- Mechanic (game canon): Only specific units and structures can see cloaked and burrowed units; in SC2 they also expose hallucinations. Each army must bring its own detector or it cannot fight hidden enemies at all.
- Counterpart (text): Balaam's donkey sees the angel standing in the road that Balaam cannot see, until the LORD opens his eyes; Elisha's servant is shown the hidden host. Paul: to another the distinguishing of spirits; the eye cannot say to the hand, 'I have no need of you'.
- Citation: Num 22:23-31; 2 Kgs 6:17; 1 Cor 12:10, 12:21
- Invariant (interpretation): Sight is observer-relative. Seeing what is hidden is a specialist faculty that some members have and others lack; the whole body depends on it; and it can be granted.
- Residual: 1 Corinthians 12:10 ('distinguishing between spirits') is about judging true from false, which matches detection's exposure of hallucinations in SC2 but not its exposure of cloaked presence. The 'eyes opened' texts (Numbers 22, 2 Kings 6) carry the presence half. Detection does not expose Changelings (SC2-Z06), so discernment is not reducible to a sensor.
- Sources: sc2/Detector, bw/Detection, sc2/Observer (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Overseer (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Raven (Legacy of the Void), bw/Science Vessel, bw/Overlord, sc2/Missile Turret (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Spore Crawler (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Photon Cannon (Legacy of the Void)

### Context rows (not STRONG; not promoted)

#### PASS-04 — All races: Cloaking and Burrow [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Cloaked or burrowed units cannot be seen or targeted except by detection.
- Counterpart (text): If they dig into Sheol, if they climb to heaven, if they hide on Carmel or at the bottom of the sea, I will search them out.
- Citation: Amos 9:2-3; Ps 139:7-12; Heb 4:13
- Invariant (interpretation): Every concealment mode is relative to an observer; an observer with full sight defeats all of them.
- Residual: Amos lists hiding modes (dig down, climb up, the sea floor) that read like burrow and air. But the texts say hiding from God never works, while the game makes hiding work against most units. Strong as a contrast; PARTIAL as a mapping.
- Sources: sc2/Cloak, sc2/Burrow, bw/Burrow

#### SC2-T08 — Ghost: Cloak [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Turns invisible while energy lasts; only detectors or reveal effects can see or target it.
- Counterpart (text): Hiding is observer-relative: hidden from some eyes, never from God's.
- Citation: Gen 3:8-10; Ps 139:7-12; Heb 4:13
- Invariant (interpretation): Concealment holds only against observers who lack the needed sight.
- Residual: In the game concealment usually works; in the texts hiding from God never works. Concealment from a human is relative, which matches; concealment from God is absolute, which does not. Detection (PASS-03) carries the strong half of this pair.
- Sources: sc2/Ghost (Legacy of the Void), sc2/Cloak

#### SC2-T30 — Orbital Command (BW: Comsat Station): Scanner Sweep [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Spends energy to reveal any spot on the map for a short time, including cloaked, burrowed and hallucinated units.
- Counterpart (text): Eyes opened for a moment to see the hidden host.
- Citation: 2 Kgs 6:17
- Invariant (interpretation): Sight that defeats concealment can be granted temporarily to someone who lacks it.
- Residual: Elisha prays and the servant sees; the scan is purchased with energy and aimed by the player. The 'granted sight' structure matches; the giver and the price do not.
- Sources: sc2/Orbital Command (Legacy of the Void), bw/Comsat Station

#### BW-T04 — Medic: Optical Flare [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Permanently reduces one unit's sight range to 1 and removes its detection.
- Counterpart (text): 'Strike this people with blindness', and the army that came to seize Elisha is led away.
- Citation: 2 Kgs 6:18-20
- Invariant (interpretation): Blind the enemy's eyes so that what is hidden stays hidden.
- Residual: Elisha's blinding is of a whole army and is lifted; Optical Flare is single-target and permanent. Used to blind detectors, it protects cloaked units, which is the same strategic use as 2 Kings 6.
- Sources: bw/Medic

#### SC2-P19 — Oracle: Revelation [PARTIAL]
- Mechanic (game canon): Enemy units and structures in an area grant vision for 20 s and lose cloak and burrow; the mark follows them as they move.
- Counterpart (text): Nothing is covered that will not be revealed; the Lord will bring to light what is hidden.
- Citation: Luke 12:2; 1 Cor 4:5
- Invariant (interpretation): Exposure that persists after the moment of revealing.
- Residual: The name is borrowed. Luke 12:2 and 1 Corinthians 4:5 describe a final, total uncovering by God; Revelation is local and lasts 20 seconds.
- Flags: NAME_BORROWING
- Sources: sc2/Oracle (Legacy of the Void)

### Grading rule
STRONG needs three or more shared causal features, a text that itself describes the structure, and survival of the recorded disanalogy. Names borrowed from religious vocabulary earn nothing.
